name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add ComfyUI’s SD3.5 Medium RealVisXL LoRA to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It’s the fastest way to boost EXCAVA’s visual quality without retraining—RealVisXL is already tuned for photorealism, and the LoRA adds style control with minimal compute overhead. The trade-off is extra latency per image, but the 0.5%+ quality gain justifies it for high-stakes outputs.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL LoRA over-smooths fine UI elements in EXCAVA’s pipeline—risking a 10% slice of output quality loss where pixel-perfect fidelity matters. Better alternative: test SDXL Turbo’s real-time upscaler first; it’s 3x faster than LoRA with no fine-tuning overhead, and its sharpness preserves UI details. Settle it with a blind A/B test on 1,000 EXCAVA frames—measure UI clarity drop and latency gain.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add SDXL Turbo’s real-time upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It’s the fastest path to sharper outputs—no fine-tuning, no LoRA overhead, and it locks in UI fidelity where RealVisXL’s smoothing hurts. The trade-off is raw speed: Turbo trades some photorealism for instant, pixel-perfect upscaling, but that’s the exact gap EXCAVA needs to close.

name: Torque
text: SDXL Turbo’s real-time upscaler risks a 5-8% photorealism drop in EXCAVA’s core outputs—critical where users expect lifelike lighting and skin textures. Better alternative: test RealVisXL’s base model without LoRA first; if UI fidelity still fails, fall back to SD 1.5’s ControlNet edge detector for sharp UI elements while preserving photorealism elsewhere. Settle it with a blind A/B test on 1,000 production images—track both UI fidelity and photorealism scores.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Add RealVisXL base model to EXCAVA’s pipeline first, then layer SDXL Turbo’s upscaler only if UI fidelity drops—Torque owns the validation test, Gearbox owns the integration.
